text:
maria_infra: Heads-up — after the driver/roi-kernel roll yesterday on sfo-gpu-02 we see a ~20% throughput drop for batched text-gen (seq=1024, batch=8). P95 latency also moved from ~120ms to ~260ms. Can someone take a look?

sam_sre: Ack. Saw alerts from CI bench too. Do you have the perf numbers and which kernel/driver landed?

maria_infra: Driver: nvidia-driver-535.33 -> 536.21, kernel: 5.19.0-54 -> 5.19.0-55. Quick numbers from yesterday's job:
```
model: opt-1.3b-8bit
seq: 1024
batch: 8
tokens/s before: 78k
tokens/s after: 62k
p95 latency before: 120ms
p95 latency after: 260ms
```
Seems reproducible on sfo-gpu-02 and sfo-gpu-05 (same node image).

henry_hw: @maria_infra can you paste nvidia-smi/topology and dmesg around the run? Curious if MIG or ECC stuff changed. Also any kernel trace logs?

maria_infra: pasted below — dmesg has a recurring kernelWARN about "attempted stall" from nv-host, and a bunch of sg_dma_map warnings. nvidia-smi shows all GPUs in-use and temps normal.
```
# dmesg | tail -n 30
[10234.123456] nv-host: attempt to schedule stalled work: queue=3
[10234.123789] sg: sg_dma_map: scatter-gather chain length exceeded
[10234.124000] audit: type=1400 apparmor="DENIED" operation="mprotect" cmdline="python" 
```

sam_sre: sg_dma_map warnings -> that smells like a driver change to scatter-gather/PCIe mapping. Could be kernel/driver combo exposing a regression in our large KV cache transfers (big tensors).

ci-bench: Automated CI benchmark reproduces the drop on sfo-image-2026-03-10 with 536.21 driver. Quick diff from microbench: memcpy throughput on GPU -> -18%, small kernel launch overhead -> +1.6x.

alex_oncall: If it's a driver regression we should consider rollback on the Dedicated pool, but let's confirm scope first. Can we run a targeted microbench and a soak on one node? Steps: 1) run small memcpy and kernel latency test, 2) run end-to-end batched gen for 30m, 3) collect perf counters and dmesg. Who can run?

maria_infra: I'll run the tests now on sfo-gpu-02. Posting commands I run so it's reproducible:
```
# microbench
ssh sfo-gpu-02
python -m bench.cuda_memcpy --size 4G --iters 50 > /tmp/memcpy.log
python -m bench.kernel_latency --iters 10000 > /tmp/kernel_latency.log
# e2e
./runtests/throughput.sh --model opt-1.3b --seq 1024 --batch 8 --duration 1800 --out /tmp/e2e.log
sudo dmesg -T > /tmp/dmesg.post
sudo nvidia-smi -q > /tmp/nvidia-smilog
```

jen_prod: FYI we have traffic routed to Dedicated capacity in SFO for a few customers — if we end up rolling back drivers that'll affect other tenants. We should coordinate a short maintenance window if rollback needed.

maria_infra: Results so far (first 12 minutes): memcpy throughput -17%, kernel latency median +40%, e2e tokens/s matches CI: ~62k. dmesg shows same sg_dma_map warnings.

henry_hw: Next hypothesis: PCIe MTU/offload change or kernel scatter-gather limit. Check /proc/bus/pci/devices and /sys/module/sg/parameters/max_segments. Also confirm no recent firmware blob change on NICs that could affect DMA mapping.

maria_infra: checked sg param: /sys/module/sg/parameters/sg_max_sectors shows 128 (same as baseline). PCI config looks unchanged. NIC firmware unchanged per fw-report.

sam_sre: Good. Two parallel experiments: A) try older driver (reinstall 535.33) on a single node and rerun e2e soak to see if throughput returns. B) instrument model runtime to force smaller KV transfers (smaller batch accumulation) to see if throughput improves — helps narrow if it's scatter-gather size. Can someone own A?

alex_oncall: I'll take A. Reverting driver on sfo-gpu-05 now and will run same e2e for 30m. Rolling revert will be scheduled only on two nodes for now.

deploy-bot: Revert package deployment queued: revert-nvidia-driver-53621 -> 53533 on sfo-gpu-05 (ID: rb-2026-17755). ETA to complete: 4m.

alex_oncall: Revert completed on sfo-gpu-05. Running e2e...

ci-bench: Early numbers from sfo-gpu-05 (reverted): tokens/s = 79k, p95 = 125ms. Matches pre-roll baseline within noise.

maria_infra: OK looks like driver regression. Action items: 1) pin Dedicated node images back to driver 535.33 until driver vendor patch; 2) block auto-upgrade pipeline for gpu images; 3) rollout plan for customer-impacting nodes if vendor releases fix. I'll start a handoff doc and a short runbook for oncall.

sam_sre: +1. Also add a short perf-validation checklist to eng-infra runbook repo. Minimum checks: memcpy microbench, kernel latency, dmesg scan for sg warnings, tokens/s for a 30m soak. Include commands above.

jen_prod: I'll coordinate a 20-minute maintenance window with accounts that might be affected and send an email with rollback notice.

maria_infra: Handoff summary (copy this into the runbook and paste into the incident tracker):
```
- Incident: throughput regression on SFO Dedicated after driver 536.21 + kernel 5.19.0-55
- Impact: ~20% throughput drop for batched gen workloads, P95 latency increase ~2x
- Cause: regression in NVIDIA driver 536.21 (scatter-gather / DMA behavior)
- Mitigation: reverted driver on subset of nodes -> restored perf
- Next: pin images, block auto-upgrades, vendor escalation ticket opened (NV-INC-2026-0456)
- Runbook checks: memcpy microbench, kernel latency, 30m e2e soak, dmesg grep for sg_dma_map
- Contacts: maria_infra, sam_sre, alex_oncall, henry_hw
```

alex_oncall: I've created a PR to pin the sfo-dedicated image and a rollback playbook. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/image-pin/pull/212

henry_hw: Will open a vendor debug session with NV support and attach logs. NV ticket: NV-INC-2026-0456.

sam_sre: Great. Closing thread for now — tracking in incidents/1775500000 and runbook updates. Reopen if we see recurrence after vendor update. :white_check_mark:
